title: Will the following years be the warmest year on record, according to NASA?
resolution_criteria: Each sub-question resolves "Yes" if [NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-analysis-confirms-2023-as-warmest-year-on-record/) officially reports that the year is the hottest year on record to date. It resolves "No" otherwise.
background: 2023 was the [hottest year on record](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-analysis-confirms-2023-as-warmest-year-on-record/), exacerbated by human-made climate change and El Niño. Despite setting new temperature highs in 2023, predictions for 2024 and beyond are uncertain due to the irregular behaviour of the current El Niño.

* 2026 now has roughly a 93% chance of becoming the warmest year on record, up from about 69% a month ago.

But assume that is out of date now

comments.author: mmmeta
comments.text: @(alt) that dashboard uses the era5 model, the resolution source is nasa gistemp data, though. Key assumptions are very different between those two, e.g. how ocean temperature is treated (nasa: water temperature, era5: air 2m over the water). Overall, I wouldn't put that much weight on this dashboard's forecast values for this question. Berkeley Earth is methodologically much closer to nasa gistemp and the better proxy.
